title: Module stalk comparison and geometric-fibre restriction factorization
statement: Let f:X -> Y be quasi-compact and quasi-separated, s:Spec Omega -> Y a geometric point with Omega algebraically closed, F an etale sheaf of Lambda-modules [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], and (g′:X′ -> X,f′:X′ -> Spec Omega,f,s) Cartesian [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Let A be the pointed-neighbourhood ring colimit [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], with any IsLocalRing structure, and rho:Spec A -> Y its structural map [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map]. Put T=X times_Y Spec A, with projections q:T -> X and p:T -> Spec A. There exist t:Spec Omega -> Spec A with t rho=s and image the closed point, and i:X′ -> T with i q=g′ and (i,f′,p,t) Cartesian. There are module isomorphisms Theta:(f_*F)_s -> Gamma(T,q^*F) and b:Gamma(X′,i^*q^*F) -> (g′^*F)(id_X′), such that for every pointed etale neighbourhood (V,v) and section z in F(V times_Y X), b applied to restriction along i of Theta(germ(z)) equals the inverse-image unit restriction along the iterated pullback lift with projections (f′ followed by v,g′) and id_X′. This statement asserts no injectivity of the restriction along i and imposes no integral or proper hypothesis.

source.place: Tags 03Q9 and 03Q1; strict henselization construction in Tag 04HX

proof.text: Use the marked maps from Spec Omega to the affine pointed neighbourhoods to form a cone, and take its unique map t to the strict-henselization limit. Cone compatibility gives t rho=s. The closed-fibre theorem, applied to the image of t, proves it is the closed point of Spec A. Take i to be the unique pullback lift with projections g′ and f′ followed by t. Pullback pasting proves (i,f′,p,t) Cartesian.

Apply the canonical set-valued pushforward-stalk comparison to the underlying set sheaf. Forgetting modules preserves the filtered stalk colimit and commutes with inverse images and their units. The representative formula is linear, so the comparison lifts to a bijective linear map Theta, hence a module isomorphism to Gamma(T,q^*F), using evaluation at the terminal etale object. Affine pointed neighbourhood cofinality extends the representative formula to every V,v.

From i q=g′, use inverse-image composition to identify i^* q^* F with g′^* F. Compose its global sections with the terminal-section isomorphism to obtain b. Naturality and composition of units identify b after restriction along i after Theta with the unit restriction along the iterated pointed lift: the two maps have first projection (f′ followed by v,g′) and second projection id_X′, hence agree by pullback uniqueness. This proves the displayed representative formula without any integral hypothesis.
